title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1RC0RA_0LA0LE_1LC1RF_1LA1LC_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1RC0RA_0LA0LE_1LC1RF_1LA1LC_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is made of epochs that each make the tape about 5/3 times longer (seen to 1010 steps, 15 epochs); the machine can only stop on A> 1 1 1, which the long (10)n/(1100)m body never contains, so the halting question is about the small irregular region at the left end, whose evolution is not understood. Lean proves the three shift rules that move the head across the body.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules across the body
claims.text: B> (10)n becomes (01)n B> in 2n steps, A> (01)n becomes (10)n A> in 2n steps, and C travels left through (1010)n carrying a 0 1 defect, leaving the body as it was, in 10n steps.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F reading 1; F is entered only from D reading 1, and D only from A reading 1, so the machine halts exactly when A reads the first of three 1s in a row (A> 1 1 1). Neither (10)n nor (1100)m contains 111.
claims.where: read off the table (only F1 halts: step_none_iff, lean/Blank.lean)

claims.title: Epochs to 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: An epoch begins with a sweep across at least 80% of the tape. Epochs begin at steps 23, 2,421, 15,052, 100,618, 213,384, 514,417, 1,329,037, 3,738,738, 19,372,038, 32,388,399, 70,752,889, 172,844,740, 454,817,413, 1,259,326,927 and 6,311,514,639, with the right end of the tape at 5, 31, 118, 284, 556, 1,017, 1,793, 3,126, 4,946, 7,969, 13,277, 22,192, 37,035, 61,817, 94,515 cells. In regular epochs the right end grows by a factor 1.67 and the time by about 2.7 (close to (5/3)<sup>2</sup>); the irregular ones (factor 5 in time) are those in which the left end moved (199 to 283, 386 to 438 cells left of the start).

claims.title: How an epoch works
claims.text: Inside an epoch an active zone of (10)n is born at the right end and widens leftward into a region of (1100)m; the head bounces inside the zone (B going right shifts the body by a cell, C going left carries a 0 1 defect), each bounce adding 3 cells at the right end. When the zone reaches the left end, a few full-width sweeps pack (10)(10) into 1100 and unpack it again, the left region is rewritten, and a new zone starts. Observed in space-time diagrams and tape dumps, not proved.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with windows K = 3, 4, 5, 6 finds no closed set that excludes halting (12, 48, 192 and 384 abstract halting configurations remain). The n-gram CPS decider (widths 3 to 7, with history and LRU augmentations) also fails.
claims.where: tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py; the n-gram run of group G02 (not in the repo)

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 57,080 cells have been visited and 28,533 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.615).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs A> 1 1 1, which can only appear in the irregular region at the left end (or in the short-lived debris that the packing sweeps leave); that region changes only once every few epochs and its rule has not been found.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 57,080 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A long striped body and a small tangle at the left
html:
Write a for the two cells 10 and b for the four cells 1100. At step 1,001,933 the whole tape (2,000 cells) reads

a 0 b^173 1 1 [A0] 0 a^5 0 a^2 1 a^519 1

On the left, 173 copies of 1100; then a short tangle where the head is; then 519 copies of 10 and a final 1. At almost any moment the tape is like this: a few hundred irregular cells at the left end (the part that grows like a logarithm), then a body made of 10 and 1100 that is tens of thousands of cells long (the part that grows like a square root).

sections.heading: Three ways across the body
html: In state B the head runs right over 10 10 10 ... two cells per two steps, turning each 10 into 01: the stripes are shifted one cell. State A does the reverse over 01 01 .... Going left, state C carries a small defect 0 1 through 10 10 10 10 at four cells per ten steps and leaves the stripes as they were. These three facts are proved in Lean (lean/Rules.lean).
A trace of the leftward glider (the head is in brackets): 1010101010101010[C0]1 becomes, ten steps later, 1010101010[C0]11010: the defect has moved four cells left, nothing else changed.

sections.heading: Epochs, each 5/3 as long
html: The run is a sequence of epochs. An epoch starts with an active zone of stripes (10)n at the right end of the tape. The head bounces inside the zone; every bounce adds three cells at the right end and pushes the zone's left edge further left into the packed region (1100)m. In the space-time diagram each epoch is a parabola-shaped region opening downward. When the zone reaches the tangle at the left end, the head makes a few sweeps across the whole tape, packing 10 10 into 1100 on the way right and unpacking on the way left, the tangle is rewritten, and a new epoch starts.

Epochs started at steps 100,618, 213,384, 514,417, 1,329,037, 3,738,738, ... 1,259,326,927 and 6,311,514,639; the tape's right end was at 284, 556, 1,017, 1,793, 3,126, ... 61,817 and 94,515. In a regular epoch the tape grows by a factor of about 5/3 and the epoch lasts about (5/3)2 times as long as the last one, which is why the right side grows like the square root of time.

sections.heading: Only on three 1s in a row
html: The machine stops only when F reads a 1. F is reached only from D reading a 1 and D only from A reading a 1, so it stops exactly when A reads the first of three consecutive 1s. The body (10 and 1100) never has three 1s in a row; only the tangle at the left end and the short debris around the head during packing sweeps can. Whether the tangle ever produces A> 1 1 1 is the whole question, and the tangle's rule from one epoch to the next was not found: it is rewritten only in some epochs (the left end moved at steps around 4·106, 1.4·109 and 6·109).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.615).
After 109 steps the tape spans 57,080 cells (283 left of the start, 39,192 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A body of (10)^n that is repeatedly packed into (1100)^m and unpacked again by sweeps, in epochs that each grow the tape by a factor about 5/3, with a small irregular region at the left end that grows only in some epochs.
